it is here believed that the ’ rafting process after 5 hours in creep in this area under the investigated conditions coalescence is governed first by the release of the elastic energy (i.e. induced by the inhomogeneity in phases stiffnesses and /’ coherency ) and then by the creep deformation.

The ’ rafting orientation correlates in a very satisfying way to the spatial evolution of the local stress triaxiality obtained by using a viscoplastic finite element simulation of the stress field evolution in the creep specimens.

This faster morphological evolution may result from the fact that in compression creep, the  channels widening is slower (as shown in this work), leading to a higher density of vertical  channels where dislocations mainly glides in the first part of creep deformation , and hence, to a higher probability of ’ rafts interconnections.
